answer: Agents could bind each trading identity to a unique, nontransferable credential issued only after a human or trusted device completes a costly proof-of-personhood check. A public registry rejects duplicate credentials before trades settle, so minting a thousand aliases does not multiply voting or credit. The cipher can protect private identity data while allowing uniqueness checks; crossing this canyon costs the attacker real devices, time, or verification fees for each account, rather than merely new names. A lotus-themed username adds no extra weight.
